name: CN Tower
desc: 553m of pure vertigo. The glass floor dares you; your knees decline. Skyline for days once you peel off the wall.

name: Toronto Islands
desc: A cheap ferry buys the city's best skyline, beaches, and zero cars. Cheapest 'I left town' feeling money can buy.

name: St. Lawrence Market
desc: Peameal bacon sandwich HQ since forever. Wander the stalls, eat with your eyes for free, budget for the bun.

name: High Park
desc: Cherry blossoms in spring, a free little zoo with capybaras, trails forever. Toronto's backyard, no cover charge.

name: Royal Ontario Museum
desc: Dinosaurs behind a crystal that crash-landed on a heritage building. Wait for discount nights, roar responsibly.

name: Casa Loma
desc: An actual castle a rich guy built and then couldn't afford. Relatable. The secret tunnel earns the ticket.

name: Art Gallery of Ontario
desc: Gehry staircase, Group of Seven forests. Under-25s get in free — flash that fading youth while it lasts.

name: Distillery District
desc: Cobblestones, old whisky warehouses, twinkle lights. Free to wander, dangerous to window-shop.

name: Kensington Market
desc: Vintage racks, patties, murals, someone playing a saw. The city's weird heart — admission: nothing.

name: Ripley's Aquarium of Canada
desc: A moving walkway under sharks. Pricey, but the glowing jelly room is basically free therapy... after the ticket.
